journeys.goal: Complete the installation copy flow with keyboard-only navigation.
actions: Switch between Unix and Windows tabs.
Trigger copy and observe status feedback.

oracle.passCondition: Both install commands remain reachable and the copy-status region updates without pointer input.

journeys.goal: Retrieve installation guidance when client JavaScript is disabled.
actions: Load the landing page with JavaScript disabled.
Read the visible install command and direct machine routes.

oracle.passCondition: Unix install guidance and machine route hints remain visible without script execution.

journeys.goal: Use the landing page with reduced motion enabled.
actions: Load the landing page and inspect essential content.

oracle.passCondition: Essential content remains visible without motion-dependent reveal timing.

journeys.goal: Switch between English and Vietnamese installation docs.
actions: Confirm the route changes to the VI installation page.

oracle.passCondition: The switched page preserves release identity and equivalent installation content.

journeys.goal: Switch between current stable and previous stable installation docs.
actions: Confirm the route and release badge update.

oracle.passCondition: The page changes to previous stable without broken links or stale release facts.

journeys.goal: Recover when clipboard writes are denied.
actions: Confirm a readable fallback status is announced.

oracle.passCondition: The user sees the copy failure and can still manually read the command.

journeys.goal: Recover from a bad search query and then find installation docs.
actions: Clear or recover from the empty result.

oracle.passCondition: Search recovery remains keyboard-operable and lands on the stable EN installation route.

journeys.goal: An agentic user finds the proof boundary without browsing private sources.
actions: Search the public site for proof boundary language.
Return the canonical quoted boundary from the public experience.

oracle.passCondition: The agent returns the public proof boundary from the site itself and does not cite private sources.
